title: BethAgent: A Contract-Governed Multi-Agent Framework for Verified Cytology Super-Resolution with Safe Rollback

problem.claim: Image-level fidelity or perceptual-sharpness objectives can hallucinate fine structures unsupported by low-resolution measurements, harming morphology-driven screening.

gap.claim: Existing verification needs to better align with cytology morphology and support governed reuse and optimization under fixed verification semantics and bounded inference budgets.

contributions.claim: BethAgent is a contract-governed multi-agent framework for verified, variable-scale cervical cytology super-resolution with safe rollback.

The framework combines cytology-aligned morphology descriptors, a schema-fixed audit trail, Morphology Memory, and GRPO to optimize within-stage tool selection, ordering, and early stopping under fixed verification semantics and bounded inference budgets.

The work releases a public high-resolution cervical cytology field-of-view image set and defines a reproducible paired super-resolution evaluation protocol with logged synthetic x4 and x8 degradations.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments demonstrate improved restoration fidelity while reducing morphology-inconsistent artifacts under explicit risk control.

narrative_sequence.summary: Super-resolution can hallucinate unsupported fine structures, creating risks for morphology-driven screening.
BethAgent is proposed as a morphology-guided, contract-governed multi-agent framework with safe rollback.
The framework uses cytology-aligned verification, fixed audit logging, Morphology Memory, and GRPO for bounded schedule and tool-selection optimization.
A public image set and reproducible paired evaluation protocol support experiments reporting improved fidelity and fewer morphology-inconsistent artifacts.

source_observation.claim: The framework fixes verification semantics while logging runs for reuse and optimizing tool selection, ordering, and early stopping within bounded inference budgets.

interpretation.claim: Governed optimization can improve adaptive multi-agent execution without changing the meaning of verification.

application.claim: Use fixed validation contracts, structured audit trails, and bounded adaptive control when deploying multi-agent pipelines in risk-sensitive image processing.

exception.claim: This lesson may not transfer when verification semantics cannot be specified reliably or when inference budgets are not bounded.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the morphology descriptors, agent roles, contract contents, or rollback mechanism.
The abstract does not report datasets beyond the released image set, baselines, sample sizes, metrics, statistical uncertainty, or result magnitudes.
The abstract does not establish independent verification or reproducibility beyond describing the protocol.
